audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 12, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness and political-theology audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for labor grievance, servant leadership, generational stereotyping, masculinity and sexualized threat, violent coercion, providence language, worker revolt, Adoram's death, civil-war mobilization, prophetic de-escalation, religious centralization, golden calves, priestly class, and political fear.

verses.restored: Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel came to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard—while still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon and lived—
they sent and called him. Jeroboam and all assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying:
Your father made our yoke hard. Now lighten hard service of your father and heavy yoke he placed upon us, and we will serve you.
He said, Go for three days, then return to me. The people went.
King Rehoboam consulted elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he lived, saying, How do you counsel me to answer this people?
They spoke to him, If today you become servant to this people, serve them, answer them, and speak good words, they will be your servants all days.
But he abandoned counsel elders gave and consulted young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.
He said to them, What counsel do you give, that we may answer this people who said, Lighten yoke your father placed upon us?
Young men who grew with him said, Thus say to this people: My father made your yoke heavy, but you say, Lighten it. Thus say: My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
Now, my father loaded you with heavy yoke, and I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.
Jeroboam and all people came to Rehoboam on third day, as king spoke, Return to me on third day.
The king answered people harshly and abandoned counsel elders gave.
He spoke according to counsel of young men: My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.
The king did not listen to people, for turn of events was from YHWH, to establish word YHWH spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

All Israel saw king did not listen. People answered king: What portion have we in David? No inheritance in son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel. Now see to your own house, David. Israel went to their tents.
But Rehoboam reigned over children of Israel living in cities of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over forced labor, and all Israel stoned him with stones and he died. King Rehoboam hurried to mount chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
Israel rebelled against house of David until this day.
When all Israel heard Jeroboam returned, they sent and called him to assembly and made him king over all Israel. None followed house of David except tribe of Judah.
Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and assembled all house of Judah and tribe of Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight house of Israel and return kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
Word of Divine came to Shemaiah, man of Divine, saying:
Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, all house of Judah and Benjamin, and remainder of people, saying:

Thus says YHWH: You shall not go up or fight your brothers, children of Israel. Return each to his house, for this matter is from me. They listened to word of YHWH and returned to go according to word of YHWH.
Jeroboam built Shechem in hill country of Ephraim and lived there; he went from there and built Penuel.
Jeroboam said in his heart, Now kingdom may return to house of David.
If this people go up to sacrifice in house of YHWH at Jerusalem, heart of this people will return to their lord Rehoboam king of Judah; they will kill me and return to Rehoboam.
The king took counsel and made two golden calves. He said to people, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Look, your gods, Israel, who brought you up from land of Egypt.
He placed one in Bethel and one in Dan.
This matter became sin, and people went before one as far as Dan.
He made a house of high places and made priests from all ends/classes of people who were not sons of Levi.

Jeroboam made a feast in eighth month, fifteenth day, like feast in Judah, and went up upon altar. Thus he did in Bethel, sacrificing to calves he made, and stationed in Bethel priests of high places he made.
He went up upon altar he made in Bethel on fifteenth day of eighth month, month he devised from his heart. He made a feast for children of Israel, went up upon altar, and burned incense.

translation_notes: The northern assembly's complaint is a labor and taxation grievance: Solomon's service and yoke were heavy. The kingdom divides after the new ruler refuses material relief.
The elders advise servant leadership, but their phrase that the people will then be servants forever still reflects hierarchy rather than democratic equality.
The problem is not that advisors are young. It is that Rehoboam chooses peers insulated by privilege who recommend humiliation and intensified coercion.
The little-finger/loins boast and scorpion threat are sexualized masculinity and torture rhetoric. They should not be admired as strength.
Providence language in verse 15 does not erase Rehoboam's deliberate refusal, advisor responsibility, or the people's valid grievance.
Adoram is killed as the official embodiment of forced labor. Worker revolt does not make mob killing harmless, and his death does not erase the system he administered.
The word through Shemaiah stops a civil war between kin. Divine speech functions here as de-escalation rather than battle authorization.
Jeroboam's fear of losing political loyalty leads him to redesign worship. Accessibility concerns about traveling to Jerusalem are real, but they are manipulated to secure his throne.
Calling non-Levite priests 'from the lowest people' in some translations reinforces class contempt. The Hebrew more likely means from the whole/ends of the people.
The critique of Bethel and Dan must not become contempt for later Samaritans, present-day religious minorities, or non-centralized worship.
safety_note: Center the workers' demand to lighten the yoke. Do not glorify authoritarian masculinity, torture threats, mob killing, civil war, or religious monopoly. Providence does not cancel human accountability, and accessible worship must not be manipulated for regime security.
